column31:
After event ingestion, the pipeline mechanism is dynamically configured using event filters. If the filter passes, the event is processed by an EventFactory, which may generate a new, follow-up event, which is fed into the same mechanism until a fixed point is reached. (These EventFactories may generate side-effects like e-mails.) This is re-use, as any of these blocks can be combined.

This results in raw event logs, which feed into a secondary pipeline system, running a pre-defined set of all mathematically interesting operators (sum, min, max, avg, count) and materialize results for the lowest temporal resolution. This is implemented purely in SQL for reasons of efficiency, using the same re-usable generic trigger-generation code for any event log. These results trigger aggregation steps at the next, higher temporal resolution, generating another materialized view, and so on. This limits us to operators which can be aggregated at a higher level, but allow for a tremendous amount of code-reuse, of which we can be quite certain that it is correct.
